task.description: Re-gate the reworked docs/agents/design/ISS-0020-fix.md (Sec2/2.1/2.2) that CODE-DESIGNER produced to close ISS-0020-SEC-1, the MEDIUM timing side-channel SECURITY-REVIEWER found in the previously-implemented guard-clause shape.
acceptance_criteria: The blocked branch and the not-blocked branch perform the same DB read (resolveLangForTg) and exactly one Telegram Bot API network round-trip each, before notificationFailed is resolved and ctx.reply is reached, in both makeStaffAddHandler and makeStaffRemoveHandler
Zero ctx.api.sendMessage calls still occur for a blocked EventStaff target
The mechanism is justified against alternatives with explicit reasoning, and any residual timing difference is stated rather than silently claimed away
No new implementation code in the design doc

result.summary:
Read docs/agents/design/ISS-0020-fix.md's current (reworked) Sec0-Sec5 in full independently, cross-checked against handoffs/ISS-0020/step-03c-security-reviewer.json's original FAIL and handoffs/ISS-0020/step-02-code-designer-rework1.json's stated intent, and re-derived each check against the artefact itself rather than trusting the rework summary.

1. TIMING LEAK ACTUALLY CLOSED (not just narrowed) -- PASS, with the disclosure quality itself checked. Sec2.1's table gives both branches the identical sequence: (1) await resolveLangForTg, (2) compose body, (3) exactly one awaited Bot API network round-trip (getMe() vs sendMessage()), (4) resolve notificationFailed. This closes the CATEGORICAL asymmetry SEC-1 flagged (zero network calls vs one) -- the actual defect named in the FAIL, which was a discrete zero-vs-one gap, not a demand for byte-identical timing. Sec2.2 explicitly separates 'equalized' (the categorical gap) from 'not claimed equalized' (getMe() vs sendMessage() differ in payload size and server-side handling, so a patient statistical attacker averaging many samples could in principle still detect a difference) and states this is a proportional, not swept-under-the-rug, call for a MEDIUM-severity, narrow-threat-model fix (an already-authorized organizer probing one target's blocked flag). This is honest disclosure, not overclaiming -- confirmed by reading Sec2.2 and Sec5 item 3 directly, both of which name the residual rather than asserting full closure anywhere in the document. Judged reasonable and non-blocking: the residual is a sub-network-round-trip statistical signal requiring many repeated samples, against a threat actor who already holds legitimate staff-assignment authority over that chapter -- proportionate to MEDIUM severity.

2. getMe() SIDE-EFFECT-FREE CLAIM -- verified independently, not trusted. getMe() is a read-only, argument-less Bot API method that returns the bot's own identity; it performs no send, no state mutation, no target addressing. On rate limiting: Telegram's Bot API rate limits that matter for message delivery (per-chat/per-second send throttling, the 30 msg/sec global send ceiling) are scoped to sendMessage and other content-delivery methods, not to metadata calls like getMe() -- calling getMe() does not consume or interact with the send-rate budget shared with real sends, so it introduces no new resource-contention or delivery-delay side effect. No other observable side effect exists (nothing written, nothing logged, no third party addressed). Design's characterization holds.

3. S10 ZERO-DELIVERY GUARANTEE PRESERVED -- PASS. Sec2.1's table row 3 is unambiguous: blocked branch calls ctx.api.getMe() (targets no user, discards result); not-blocked branch calls ctx.api.sendMessage(Number(targetUser.tgId), body) exactly as today. No code path in the reworked design routes a real sendMessage call, to the blocked target or to anyone else, on the blocked branch -- zero delivery, zero leaked-to-third-party risk, confirmed by reading the table's branch column, not by trusting the rework summary's restatement of it.

4. notificationFailed FORCED TRUE, NOT SHORT-CIRCUITED BY THE SHARED TRY -- PASS. Table row 4 states notificationFailed is set unconditionally immediately after the blocked branch's getMe() await settles (i.e., on the synchronous-success path, not inside any conditional), and separately notes that if getMe() itself throws, the shared catch block (unchanged, wraps the whole try) also sets notificationFailed = true -- a redundant, not conflicting, assignment. Both of the try block's exit paths for the blocked branch (falls through normally / throws) converge on notificationFailed = true; nothing in the design reintroduces a path where the blocked branch could exit with notificationFailed still false. Traced this explicitly rather than accepting the design's own 'no new branch needed' claim at face value -- it holds.

5. NON-BLOCKED PATH UNCHANGED -- PASS. Table's not-blocked column is identical at every step to the pre-fix/pre-rework shape (same resolveLangForTg call, same body composition, same sendMessage call, same catch behavior) -- confirmed against the still-live FAILed implementation in apps/bot/src/handlers/staff.ts (lines 96, 101, 103 / 170, 175, 177, grepped directly) as the 'before' baseline the design claims not to disturb. No regression introduced by folding both paths into one try block.

6. SCOPE DISCIPLINE -- PASS. `git show --stat 4e19f4e` (the rework commit) touches exactly docs/agents/design/ISS-0020-fix.md and its own handoffs/ISS-0020/step-02-code-designer-rework1.json -- no apps/bot/** file touched by this design-stage rework, as expected (implementation happens after this gate). The design's own Sec2/2.1 scope statement (staff.ts + user.ts only, no ledger/schema/other-handler touch) is unchanged from the already-approved Sec0/Sec1/Sec3 and consistent with step-03c's own scope finding.

7. NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE / NO TBD -- PASS. Sec2.1's table and prose describe control-flow shape and name existing Bot API methods (ctx.api.getMe(), ctx.api.sendMessage(...)) at the same level of concreteness the original (already-gated) Sec2 used for the guard-clause shape -- no function bodies, no new types, no copy-pasteable diff. No 'TBD'/'later'/placeholder language anywhere in Sec2, Sec2.1, Sec2.2, Sec4, or Sec5 -- Sec5's three open items are each explicitly scoped as deliberately-deferred future work, not gaps in this design.

All five task acceptance criteria met. Verdict: PASS.
